task_1.title: Stop caching missing remote package lookups
task_1.description: Version 2.18.1 rolls back the 2.18.0 remote-caching change for missing packages. Latest package reference resolution should keep reusing successful remote results, but failed lookups for packages that are not available remotely should no longer be retained as cached failures, reducing stale behavior and the memory overhead introduced by caching misses.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that missing-package remote lookups are not remembered as persistent failures within a client session, so later requests can detect newly available packages and remote resolution does not retain unnecessary failure state.

expectation.grounded: For remote latest-package resolution through `get_latest_package_reference`, only successful results for a package reference on a remote should be cached and reused. If the lookup raises because the package is missing or otherwise unavailable remotely, that exception should be surfaced for the current call without being stored for reuse on subsequent calls. Upload and removal operations should not depend on explicit remote cache invalidation to clear a previously cached missing-package failure.
expectation.conceptual: When the client asks a remote for the latest package reference, successful answers may be reused, but a missing-package result must be retried on later requests instead of being treated as a permanent cached failure for that process. Package availability changes on the remote should be observable on a later lookup without extra cache-reset steps.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the lookup contract for a single successful or failing `get_latest_package_reference` call. Repeat successful lookups for the same remote and package reference should still be reusable. The fix must not require callers to add a separate cache invalidation step after remote upload or removal operations.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve existing behavior for normal successful resolution and one-off failures, while removing only the persistence of failed missing-package lookups across repeated calls. The upgrade should not add new caller actions or configuration requirements.

behavior: Repeated latest-package lookups for the same remote and package reference continue to reuse a previously successful result.
A latest-package lookup failure caused by a package not being available remotely is not cached, so a later lookup performs a fresh remote query.
After remote package availability changes, a later latest-package lookup can observe the new state instead of reusing an earlier cached missing-package failure.
Remote upload and removal operations no longer perform blanket remote cache invalidation as part of this rollback.
Sessions that encounter many missing remote packages no longer accumulate cached failure objects for those lookups.
acceptance_criteria: When a latest package reference lookup succeeds and the same lookup is requested again in the same session, it should continue to return the successful result without changing the API behavior.

When a latest package reference lookup initially fails because the package is missing on the remote, a later lookup after that package becomes available should query the remote again rather than re-raising a previously cached failure.
When many latest-package lookups miss during a session, the client should avoid retaining cached failure state for each miss as part of normal operation.
When uploads or removals occur on a remote, callers should not need a dedicated cache-reset action solely to stop reuse of an earlier missing-package failure.
